title: ES modules, CommonJS, and what changed between them

videos.script:
For its first twenty years, JavaScript had no way for one file to use another. {{globals}} A page loaded scripts one after the other, and they all shared one global scope. Two files that each defined a function called format quietly fought, and the last one loaded won.

Two answers grew up to fix that. {{cjs}} Node, in 2009, invented CommonJS: require to bring a file in, module dot exports to say what a file offers. {{esm}} Then in 2015 the language itself got modules: import and export, the same in the browser and in Node.

Both are everywhere today. {{both}} Libraries ship one or the other or both, and older Node code is almost all CommonJS. So this lesson teaches you to read either, and to know which one you are looking at.

{{differences}} The differences matter more than the syntax. One gives you a live view of another file's variable; the other gives you a copy. One is decided before the program runs; the other while it runs. {{answers}} And they answer two old questions from earlier lessons: why each Node file had a scope of its own, and why this at the top of a file printed an empty object.
